dedupe_keys.name: cascading effects of critical infrastructure service failure in medellin interviews focus groups and interactive learning data

description: These three linked datasets document research on cascading effects of critical infrastructure service failure in hillside settlements of Medellín, Colombia, exposed to torrential rainfall and landslides. The first holds qualitative data from expert interviews, key informant interviews with community leaders and focus group discussions in one formal and one informal settlement, used with a systems thinking approach to test whether services in informal settlements are more likely to fail and cascade. The second and third hold data from interactive learning process workshops that aimed to improve citizen and community understanding of cascading effects, including critical infrastructure service matrices, pre- and post-workshop surveys, observer scores, workshop transcripts and an interview with metropolitan area officials, plus a comparison of three visualisation tools. They cover two hillside settlements and workshop groups in one city. They were produced by Deepshikha Purwar, Johannes Flacke and Richard Sliuzas at the University of Twente and published by DANS in 2025 under the DANS Licence. README files are openly downloadable, while data files (PDF transcripts and tabular survey files) are restricted and must be requested because they contain personal data. Caveats: samples are small, the data are largely qualitative, and access depends on approval. It supports cascading failure and interdependency mapping, emergency response and resilience planning for informal settlements; a related record is the Dutch critical infrastructure interdependency matrix.
